items.summary: A fresh Houthi drone and cruise-missile wave targeted the kingdom's key oil and gas facilities; several were intercepted. King Khalid airport stays closed until at least Oct 17 (NOTAM) with 46% of flights cancelled across Saudi airports; the FAA warned US airlines on Saudi routes. The World Petroleum Congress in Riyadh was disrupted — the CEOs of ExxonMobil, TotalEnergies, Shell and BP withdrew. Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdul Aziz bin Salman vowed a serious retaliation.
items.title: Oct 12: Fresh Houthi wave targets Saudi oil/gas sites; Riyadh airport shut till Oct 17, energy summit disrupted

items.summary: Turkey, Pakistan, Egypt and Saudi Arabia (the 'R4') jointly condemned the Houthi airport attacks as a 'dangerous escalation', backing all legitimate Saudi countermeasures and holding the Houthi militia fully accountable. The four signed a joint defence pact in August under which an attack on one is an attack on all; Turkey is assessing defensive/technical support for Riyadh but ruled out troop deployment and offensive operations.
items.title: Oct 12: Turkey, Pakistan, Egypt, Saudi Arabia jointly condemn attacks under defence pact
